extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry, anabelian geometry, and specialists studying Mochizuki's IUT and the abc-conjecture
extracted.subtask_short: proof of abc via arithmetic Teichmuller
extracted.subtask_description: A research-article level program constructing Arithmetic Teichmuller Spaces (arithmeticoids, holomorphoids, parameter spaces Y_L), building log-Link/global Frobenius structures and adelic Theta-sets, and using averaging/log-volume estimates to deduce Vojta’s inequality and hence the abc- and Szpiro-conjectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of arithmeticoids and arithmetic Teichmuller spaces (YL)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fixed number field is deformable: there exists a metrisable parameter space YL of arithmeticoids (deformations of the arithmetic of L) which parameterizes distinct "avatars" of the number field and for which one can speak of proximate arithmeticoids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Established in [Joshi, 2023a]; this notion captures deformations analogous to Teichmuller theory for Riemann surfaces. The underlying schemes of holomorphoids remain isomorphic to X/L while analytic/metric data vary. References: §1.1, §1.4, [Joshi, 2023a].

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a global Frobenius (log-Link) on parameter spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The parameter spaces YL (and variants Ymax_L, YR_L) carry a global Frobenius morphism ϕ (identified with Mochizuki's log-Link) whose iterates act on YL and change local valuation scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed in [Joshi, 2023a]; ϕ corresponds to Mochizuki's log-Links and its iterates produce the valuation-scaling behavior exploited in averaging arguments. See §1.5 and references to [Joshi, 2023a].

rubrics_metrics.name: Heights as functions depending on arithmeticoids (hy(x)) and product-formula compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The (logarithmic) height of an algebraic number x must be regarded as a function hy(x) depending on a chosen arithmeticoid y; local contributions change under ϕ but must satisfy a product formula for each arithmeticoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition and properties of hy(x) follow [Joshi, 2023a, Def. 8.2.1]; stability under product formula gives a period morphism YL → P(⊕v∈V L Rv). Use comparisons hy vs. hϕ(y) in height estimates (see §1.5, items (1)–(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tate-parameter behavior under Frobenius (Tate values grow under ϕ)
rubrics_metrics.description: For elliptic curves the absolute values of Tate parameters associated to holomorphoids must increase under application of the global Frobenius ϕ (this is crucial to shaving off p-powers in exponents and relating heights to conductors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an immediate consequence of [Joshi, 2023b, Theorem 10.20.1](3,4) and is discussed in §1.5(2). It explains why conductors arise naturally in the abc-context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of Initial Theta Data (Theorem 5.7.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must exist elliptic curves equipped with initial Theta-data (global assertion over number fields) needed to construct the Theta-locus Θ and carry out the adelic/Tate-parameter collation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulated and proved as Theorem 5.7.1 in this paper; corresponds to [Mochizuki, 2021d, Corollary 2.2(i,ii)]. The existence of these data is prerequisite for defining Θ_Mochizuki and Θ_Joshi (see §1.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of Mochizuki’s Adelic Ansatz ΣL' (stability under symmetries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a set ΣL' of tuples of holomorphoids (the Adelic Ansatz) which forms a configuration/correspondence on YL' and is stable under the global Frobenius ϕ and other symmetries acting on YL'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed in [Joshi, 2024c, §4.2]; ΣL' is the domain from which Tate parameters are collated into Θ-sets. Stability under ϕ is required for the iterates-invariance used in volume/height arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collation and definition of Θ_Mochizuki and Θ_Joshi (adelic Theta-sets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define adelic sets Θ_Mochizuki (and the more intrinsic Θ_Joshi) which collect tuples of Tate parameters from holomorphoids in ΣL'; these sets must be stable under iterates of the global Frobenius and encode variation of heights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction given in [Joshi, 2024c, §9] (Θ_Mochizuki) and §6 (Θ_Joshi). Θ_Mochizuki is used for upper/lower bound estimates; Θ_Joshi gives a more intrinsic description but is currently harder for direct upper bounds (see §1.5 discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper and lower bound estimates on Θ (log-volume and volume bounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain lower bounds on Vol(Θ) and upper bounds (log-volume bounds / First and Second Main Bounds) for Θ to control averaged Tate-parameters and deduce height inequalities (Vojta).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence: Existence of Initial Theta Data (Theorem 5.7.1) → use [Mochizuki, Cor.3.12]/Joshi's analogue to get lower bounds on Vol(Θ) → Theorem 6.1.1 (First Main Bound) and Theorem 6.10.1 (Second Main Bound, log-Volume) give necessary upper bounds. See §1.4 and §1.5 (ordering (1)–(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to genus-zero case with 2-adic j-invariant condition (reduction step)
rubrics_metrics.description: By Mochizuki's 2010 result, it suffices to prove the main height inequality for X = P1 and D = {0,1,∞} on compactly bounded subsets satisfying a 2-adic j-invariant condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1; see §7.1 opening lines and references to [Mochizuki, 2010]. This reduction is a standard structural step in the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Averaging/integration over arithmetic Teichmuller space (analogy with Mirzakhani)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use arithmetic analogues of volume/integration on Teichmuller spaces: average Tate-parameter-dependent functions (e.g., log of Tate) over suitable subsets of YL/Θ to obtain global bounds on heights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous to Mirzakhani's integration of geodesic-length functions; discussed in §1.5 and motivated throughout. Averaging is the central novel idea to bound height suprema via global Frobenius dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-formula hyperplane and period morphism from YL
rubrics_metrics.description: For each arithmeticoid y the product-formula defines a hyperplane Hy in ⊕v∈V L Rv; these Hy depend on y and give a non-trivial period morphism YL → P(⊕v Rv) which is used in height comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developed in [Joshi, 2023a, Theorem 5.10.1] and [Joshi, 2024c, Theorem 4.6.1]; see §1.5(5). This structure explains the global balancing of local contributions under Frobenius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical geometric description of Mochizuki’s Three Indeterminacies (Ind1, Ind2, Ind3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a canonical geometric realization/description of Mochizuki's three fundamental indeterminacies to remove doubts about their existence and role in Corollary 3.12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimed to be given in [Joshi, 2024c, §8.11] and discussed in §1.2 and §1.5; this removes ambiguities highlighted by Scholze–Stix and is needed for the construction of the Theta locus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility / reconciliation with Mochizuki’s notions (Rosetta Stone/transliteration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transliterate and reconcile the constructions in Joshi's arithmetic Teichmuller theory with Mochizuki's original terminology/objects (log-Links, Θgau-Links, Theta-values locus, Hodge Theaters, Frobenioids, etc.) so results correspond and proofs align.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'Rosetta Stone' is provided in [Joshi, 2024c, §8] and throughout this series; necessary to show that Joshi's constructions genuinely implement Mochizuki's structures and to compare corollaries (see Table 1.2.1 and §1.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and control of exceptional finite sets (Exc) and compactly bounded subsets Z
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify/construct a finite exceptional set Exc (of elliptic curves) and work with compactly bounded subsets Z so that the main bounds hold outside Exc and estimates depend controllably on Z, d, ε.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the proof of Theorem 7.1.1 (see §7.1): enlarge Exc finitely as needed to exclude curves violating bounds; height constants may depend on Z and parameters d, ε. This is a standard technical device in the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical dependency/order of results to reach the abc (reading/proof plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the specific logical sequence: (1) Existence of Initial Theta Data (Theorem 5.7.1), (2) Corollary 3.12 (volume lower bound), (3) Theorem 6.1.1 (using upper bound 6.10.1), (4) Theorem 7.1.1 (Vojta's Inequality), (5) Theorem 2.10.1 (abc and Szpiro).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given explicitly in §1.4 as the suggested reading/assimilation order; Joshi reorganizes Mochizuki's material into this more logical progression and identifies which results correspond to Mochizuki's statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Growth/control of primes and discriminant/conductor comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide prime-number bounds, global discriminant bounds, analysis of ramification and ramiﬁcation divisors, and discriminant/conductor comparisons needed to translate Tate-parameter growth into height/conductor inequalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material appears in §6 (Prime number bounds, Global Discriminant bounds, analysis of ramification) and is used in Main Bounds (Theorem 6.1.1 and 6.10.1). These technical bounds feed into the final height estimates in §7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper bound (log-Volume) and First Main Bound proofs need elementary lemmas and explicit estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove the First Main Bound (Theorem 6.1.1) and the Second Main Bound/log-Volume (Theorem 6.10.1) by assembling elementary lemmas, prime estimates, and explicit arithmetic inequalities (many lemmas and computations are required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper contains lists of easy lemmata, explicit prime and discriminant estimates, and the detailed proofs in §6 and §6.11–6.12. The proofs rely on explicit arithmetic control (e.g., Tate-size vs. conductor).
